thread:
Elena R: Quick sync: customer asked for a fully bastionless private deployment with zero mandatory outbound. They still need rapid key revocation + audit guarantees. Ideas?
Tom B: I sketched an offline-attestation model: local TPM/HSM issues an attestation blob (attest.json) that the keystore-agent uses to mint ephemeral decrypt tokens locally. Revocation handled by a signed revocation manifest (revocation.json) applied from ops when available.
Noah V: Important: the manifest must be verifiable offline. Control plane signs revocation manifest with current signing key. Agent ships a trust-bundle.pem in initial install; bundle rotation happens on reconnect.
Priya M: For RBAC, tokens minted locally should be scope-limited: audience=keystore, perms=decrypt-only, and include local-session-id. Enforce proof-of-possession (PoP) using ephemeral key in the attestation. TTL very short (<= 30s).
Elena R: How to avoid a compromised agent minting unlimited tokens while offline?
Tom B: Add two mitigations: 1) per-process token quota (cgroup enforced) 2) local rate-limiter backed by kernel (cgroup eBPF counter). If quota exceeded, agent refuses new tokens and logs the event.
Noah V: Also make cert/attest sleeps conservative: agent only mints N tokens per minute per identity. N defined by install policy.
Priya M: Audit path: every decrypt request gets an append-only local record: {ts, req_id, caller_identity_hash, op, result, seq}. Periodic signed checkpoints: agent signs checkpoint with local attestation key and writes checkpoint.meta. On reconnect, we upload the chain.
audit-bot: reminder: regulatory customers often need WORM storage for 90 days. Offline installs must negotiate SLA about audit retention.
Elena R: Network isolation: propose default namespace NetPol + egress-deny. Allowlist of egress to admin-approved proxies only. Add conntrack hard caps per namespace to protect from socket-flood.
Tom B: There's a known CVE in netlinker v2.1.3 used by the agent for conntrack controls. Short term: build agent against patched vendor fork and drop CAP_NET_ADMIN; run a small privileged helper with minimal syscalls to modify conntrack.
Noah V: Detection: eBPF program counting connects per cgroup -> metric alarm. Quick sample: 
```
# pseudo-bpf
count_connects(cgroup_id)++
if count > THRESHOLD -> push alert to local /var/run/alerts
```
and a lightweight scanner to detect rapid conntrack churn.
Priya M: Incident playbook (draft):
1) Suspected compromise -> mark identity as suspect locally (touch /var/lib/redwood/quarantine-request && sign by local admin)
2) Ops creates signed revocation manifest (S-RL) and marks identity revoked
3) Agent accepts quarantine only if local admin signature present + S-RL or control-plane signature on S-RL (two-party requirement)
4) On acceptance agent: a) kill affected worker pids b) zero out local ephemeral tokens c) escalate alert to customer contact and upload audit snapshot when network available
Elena R: Two-party approval prevents accidental mass lockouts. Nice. Make sure the local admin key is hardware-backed if present.
Tom B: Edge case: fully airgapped site where ops cannot push S-RL quickly. Local admin can still perform manual quarantine (two local admin signatures required) to avoid single-person mistakes. Record justification and signed attestations into audit logs.
Noah V: For offline log integrity, store logs in append-only file and periodically compute a rolling HMAC chain: H_i = HMAC(key, H_{i-1} || entry_i). Checkpoint signs H_i. Key derived from attestation-key. On reconnect, control plane verifies chain continuity.
Priya M: Action items:
- Tom: prepare patched agent build (drop CAP_NET_ADMIN) + privileged helper design (due EOD)
- Noah: RFC for revocation manifest format + offline trust bundle rotation (due this week)
- Elena: SLA wording for offline audit retention + customer-facing note (due tomorrow)
- Priya: Incident playbook formalization + PoP spec for tokens (due Fri)
infra-bot: deploy: keystore-agent v1.9.0-rc1 -> canary started 6161239899; logs -> /var/log/redwood/keystore-agent-canary.log
Elena R: Thanks team  please add any missing edge cases. I'll queue a walkthrough with security & solutions next week. :white_check_mark:
